question_text: A 48-year-old woman comes to the physician because of an increasingly painful swelling behind her right knee for the past 2 months. During this time, she has also had intermittent low-grade fever and she has been more fatigued than usual. She has not had any trauma to the knee. Over the past year, she has had occasional pain in her hands and wrists bilaterally. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She drinks 1–2 glasses of wine daily and occasionally more on weekends. Current medications include enalapril, metformin, and glimepiride. Her mother and older brother have osteoarthritis. She is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 68 kg (150 lb); BMI is 25 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 3-cm nontender mass in the right popliteal fossa that becomes prominent when the knee is extended. There is mild swelling and redness of her right knee joint. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient is a 48-year-old woman presenting with a painful swelling behind her right knee, intermittent low-grade fever, increased fatigue, and bilateral hand and wrist pain. The presence of a 3-cm nontender mass in the right popliteal fossa, which becomes prominent when the knee is extended, suggests a possible Baker's cyst, commonly associated with inflammatory conditions like rheumatoid arthritis. The intermittent fever and fatigue further support an inflammatory etiology. While osteoarthritis is a consideration due to her family history, the systemic symptoms and joint involvement in the hands are more indicative of rheumatoid arthritis. Psoriatic arthritis is less likely due to the absence of skin lesions. A popliteal artery aneurysm is possible but less likely given the inflammatory symptoms. Systemic lupus erythematosus is also a consideration but lacks sufficient systemic symptoms to strongly support this diagnosis. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is rheumatoid arthritis, supported by the patient's symptoms and the presence of a mass consistent with a Baker's cyst.
